- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 5–10%.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day window; add 1–2% buffer to initial forecast.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0), model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- When true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 3 consecutive days, model is biased low; increase forecast by 2–3% for next window.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.25) and model is flat, true outcome often rises; add 0.5–1% upward bias.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings >0.5, adjust forecast slope to match sentiment direction.
